title: Block: A Heap of Tuples
oneLiner: Return the k most frequent words, most frequent first and ties in alphabetical order, using a min-heap of (priority, word) tuples.
keyTakeaway: Put the whole ordering into the heap's priority as a tuple. A min-heap pops the smallest, so negate the count to get the most frequent first; the word as the second part breaks ties.
explanation:
Return the k most frequent words in words, sorted by frequency (highest first), and words with the same frequency in alphabetical order. k is at most the number of distinct words.

Count with a hashmap, then push each word with the priority (-count, word). Python's heapq compares tuples part by part, so heapq.heappush(heap, (-count, word)) and k heappops give the answer. In C#, PriorityQueue<string, (int, string)> works the same way; pass a comparer that compares the count, then the word with string.CompareOrdinal. Top K Frequent, K Closest Points and task schedulers are this block.

gotchas: Using the count as the priority in a min-heap, which pops the least frequent first.
Leaving the tiebreak out of the tuple, so equal counts come out in any order.

complexity.note: Counting is O(n); pushing up to n distinct words is O(n log n) and k pops add O(k log n). A size-k heap of the reverse order gets O(n log k).
